Stop in at the lobby of the park office to pick up a copy of the updated map showing all trails and the locations of the trail marker signs that you may encounter. Note: on the smaller trail marker signs there is a compass rosette. The rosettes have East and West switched.

Trails vary from packed dirt and gravel to grassy. Some are quite smooth, while older trails in hilly parts may have grooves worn into the trail by long-term use by horses or water erosion. In wetter seasons you may find a few muddy areas where rainfall drains or hillside springs go across the trail.

While grassy trails are normally kept mowed, long wet periods such as this spring, may let the grass get ahead of the mowers.

Be sure to wear insect protection in the form of proper clothing or application of insecticides to clothing or repellents. Ticks can be found on the grassy areas. Mid June, you'll likely encounter clouds of black flies, that may bite if you haven't take proper precautions.

Trails may be closed to horses in wetter times and are always closed to motorized vehicles.

You never know what you may encounter along the trails. I've recently came upon a recently born spotted fawn, a hen wild turkey with her small chicks, a curious deer who actually walked toward me, and a snapping turtle up on the trail laying its eggs. You'll see a variety of wild flowers. Black raspberries can be found in many places and are delicious. Common birds include bald eagles, families of Canada Geese, ducks and turkey vultures. When the trails are a little muddy it can be fun to try to identify the tracks that you find.

If you want to go completely around the lake, about the minimum distance is approximately four miles. Shorter loops of 1 to 3 miles are possible as well as longer 5 or 6 mile paths.

Paths are available all seasons. Doing the trails in winter after a fresh snow can be beautiful.

Other trail entry points include the north trailhead located near the front of the north campground and across the spillway bridge located at the far end of the dam.

Note: On the west side of the park, the hiking trails in places are very close to private and public hunting areas, which are prime deer hunting areas. - The Inn. This was truly our tipping point of why we booked this venue. It was our ideal situation to be able to host ourselves and our wedding party. It had lots of plates and cups and felt so homey. The views out back were an added plus, and was a great backdrop for our first look.

- Communication.

We stop at the West Des Moines KOA every year on our way through, and it’s easily one of the best KOAs we've stayed at! It’s a fun, clean, and family-friendly campground that always gives us a great experience.

There’s a big jump pad that my kid loves, a nice playground, and a separate toy area that keeps them entertained for hours. They’ve also got a fun water balloon fight zone and a gem mining station—so much to do! We enjoyed pizza and ice cream from the store, which is super convenient and well-stocked.

The sites are pretty wide and easy to set up in, and the staff are always so friendly and welcoming—it really makes a difference. All hotels have their bad reviews, and many people go to the extreme when posting bad reviews because they are living them experience emotionally when writing, so I don't read into the negative ratings score to seriously.

Nikki was the one who helped me at the reception area and provided me with excellent customer service. She was friendly and communicative and got me squared away quickly.

My room was also neat and clean, with a  nice smell. No weird smells as if something was being covered up. At this time of writing, nothing unusual has taken place so far, and the stay has been pleasant. When I arrived, the parking lot was nearly empty—mine was the only car. But I was told the room I picked wasn’t available… because they chose not to clean it. Not that it was booked. Not under maintenance. Just… not cleaned today.

So, I turned around and checked back out.

Just a few minutes down the road, I rebooked at The Rewind Hotel (another Hilton property). I was greeted by a friendly staff member named Jill who immediately turned the night around. She got me into exactly the kind of room I’d originally booked—end of the hallway, quieter, cleaner, calmer, and with a far better atmosphere.

And yes—the restaurant was actually open, and it’s a Johnny Italian Steakhouse.

Bottom line: I won’t be staying at this Hilton Garden Inn again. But The Rewind? 1) We were able to sign the lease quickly and efficiently.

2) The landlord, Denver, was super nice and helpful. He could be forgetful at times, but we never minded that at all. He helped with all of our maintenance needs really quickly, too. We had a microwave that had a broken handle and the couple days after notifying him, we had a brand new microwave installed.

3) We were able to hang things up on the walls. I suggest using the sticker adhesive type instead of nails though. I heard a lot of people who had to pay part of their deposit to repaint the apartment because they used nails.

4) After we lived there a year, we were able to rent monthly which made looking for a house to rent a lot easier and less stressful. We did have to pay a little extra monthly to do that, but we didn't mind.

5) Pets are aloud with a deposit. I was looking for a cat for the longest time and was I grateful I had the option to look for one in the first place.

6) The security there was the main reason I even considered this apartment. A lot of the bottom floor apartment residents just use the sliding doors as their front doors. The main building as a whole though has an intercom system, a front door that's locked at all times and the apartment itself has a deadlock. So you're given two keys plus your mail key for your apartment in total and I loved that, especially with a baby on the way. I needed that security.

7) It's super close to a lot of recreation such as the football stadium, the high school softball field and Maytag park. It was just a short walk away and I loved that.

8) A super friendly neighborhood. There's a lot of apartments in town that are located in super sketchy spots, but this one had nothing like that. It had a very friendly neighborhood vibe.

9) It does have garages you can rent alongside your normal rent so you can have extra storage on site if you needed it. I never did that, but it seems like an awesome feature.

10) I don't know about y'all but I loved the fact none of the neighbors talked to me. I lived there for a while and no one paid me any attention and as an introvert, it was great. If you like neighbors tho, this may not be your kind of place idk.

Downsides:
1) I lived under the stairs and had really noisy neighbors upstairs. The walls and floors are pretty thin in these apartments so if you have small children (which I have) that are light sleepers, I'd either invest in a loud sound machine or not recommend this apartment. Forget having your TV louder than 6 too.

2) I rented a two bedroom/ 1 bath and it was just the right size for 2 adults and a newborn, maybe even a little cramped. Anymore people and it would have been WAYYY too snug.

3) In the summer, it gets super super hot in there because of the AC unit that's only connected to the living room portion of the apartment (we solved that issue with fans) and in the winter, all of our neighbors cranked up their heat so our apartment was always hot, but we just left the windows open from time to time to make it cooler.

4) The parking lot was super cramped and the people who lived on the bottom floor never had any room to park at the bottom lot because of the rest of the residents taking those spots which ended up being super annoying because if I had a bunch of groceries, I'd have to go down stairs to get to my apartment or walk down the hill to my sliding door while also pregnant. -Reserved spot via text: kind of a neat/new aged way of reserving spots. Not sure if an online reservation program is on the radar for the future but I didn’t mind the texts.

-Pretty close to everything: grocery, golf, fishing, shopping, restaurants, etc.

-Lots of shade!

-New septic system/working towards improvements: understanding how running a business works, I saw how hard the new owners are working towards improving this campground and have already upgraded the septic system.

-Quiet: I’m an old man at heart, so I can appreciate the quiet sometimes! :)

-Full hookups: electric, water, dump station

-Firewood $1/Log: usually campgrounds will require you to pay $5-$10 for a bundle. I liked being able to grab a log or two for $1 each.

-They fill propane!: this is the first campground I’ve seen that does this. Pretty neat.

-Very engaged/approachable staff

-New owners seem to really care about improving this campground: As in any other new business ventures, it takes capital to invest capital. They seem to be putting profits back into the business. Kudos!

Work in progress:

-Roads through park are a little pitted- pretty big gravel and some pretty good sized ruts in the roads. Nothing too terrible, just more pitting and bigger gravel than I’m used to seeing in a campground.

-Dump station too high (for our camper): I had to get a little creative on how to manage dumping our tanks. Our camper sits pretty high and usually dont have a problem with this. Might just need another layer of rock or something and it’ll be just fine.

-Fire pits are a little small/can’t cook on them: some of our firewood couldn’t fit in the fire ring. Luckily we had some smaller logs to have a smaller fire. May take some time/investment to upgrade to bigger fire pits- they are still functional though!

***A little spendy for what the park has to offer compared to other campgrounds but I see the work being put into it so I really cannot say anything “negative” about this place. I always enjoy seeing people working towards their goal/passion so I am not going to point out every little flaw, rather acknowledge that this investment/vision is going to take time and will require some patience and understanding from campers in the meantime! I’m a bit late on posting this as we got married in October, and I should probably be transparent that unlike others who have left reviews, the owners were not present when we were there. HOWEVER - Jeff was extremely helpful and responsive leading up to the wedding, and would answer questions at all times of the day which I really appreciated as wedding planning is very stressful and time consuming. And this used to be their home, so I can understand why they would be protective of it - maybe just be sure to communicate your concerns from other reviews with them before making a decision, but we don’t regret a single thing about booking here.

We chose Conrad Mansion as majority of our guests were traveling from out of state, including our wedding parties, so it was really important to us to be able to spend a whole weekend with everyone. $11k may seem like a lot, but majority of other places we were looking at with the amount of people we had (about 170) were still over $9k and those were for one day only, not including stay, where as this place we could have 40 people stay with us and it was for a whole weekend. Plus the venue is STUNNING!! Mansion is a little outdated but it’s still beautiful and extremely functional. We even had our rehearsal dinner onsite and prepared our own food for it to save money (catered for actual wedding though). All of our guests absolutely loved it and all of our friends have even talked about us booking it for the future as an anniversary get together!

We really wanted an outdoor wedding (which thankful to the weather we were able to get), but it’s nice to know that when you rent this place that you get the whole property so you have a backup plan just in case, or you can even do half indoor/ half outdoor with the garages in the carriage house! The staff that were on site for day of the wedding were awesome. And I’m apart of a fire performance troupe (Sabba Circle based out of Des Moines, IA) so it was really important to me to be able to have us fire perform at our wedding which they were cool with so I think your experience can really just depend on communication! We also had my friends (from Norsefyre based out of NE) do aerialist performances during cocktail hour and while people were eating which was a dream!

So many places for beautiful photos. So many ways to customize it to how you want. They even have sheep there which is unique, and we loved that chairs, tables, outdoor games, etc were included. We’ll be reminiscing on this weekend for the rest of our lives, and we’re so thankful for the Conrad Mansion and them renting out their home to us. ❤️ little tip that helped things run super smooth for us - be sure to get your bridal/groom parties to help with clean up! Between clearing out/cleaning up when leaving and checking rooms, and especially night of the wedding when they have to clear up the carriage house, remember that many hands make light work!! Night of the wedding and leaving the carriage house before they locked it up, we literally all grabbed all of our stuff and decor like 20 minutes before they had to lock it up and just brought it outside and sorted it from there/put it in cars since we were staying there. Treat this place like your would treat your home. Made it so we could truly enjoy our whole day - and since you’re there all weekend you can set up a day or two early!!! Hope this helps, and if you’re planning your wedding, congrats! Thank you Jeff and Kim! We’ll cherish our memories there for eternity.

Sincerely,
The Barnes

At this price point (2 star motels) I’ve paid 2-1/2 times the rate in the last year for rooms FAR less comfortable and clean with lousy service.

I was greeted at the counter by a warm, friendly, courteous young man who smiled easily.
I was in a king, accessible room which was immaculately clean and unusually large.
It was clear the staff took pride in the details.
The bed was comfy with pillows that were  of varying heights and firmness so the right ones for me could be located easily.

Super 8 breakfasts vary by location and at this low a price per night, I would have expected the bare minimum.
Surprisingly, they not only offered the general fare of Belgian waffles, bagels, bread, cereal, coffee, milk and juice but also warm biscuits, sausage gravy and sausages as well.
One notes the butter was actual whipped butter-not the usual margarine that tastes like grease.
As a diabetic all I could enjoy was the coffee which was brewed strong enough that I could drink it.

Not Peets or Seattle’s Best but workable and piping hot with half and half on offer along with the usual sweetened creamers.
Again, cleanliness and care is evident in the breakfast presentation as it was in the rooms-not a given when staying at Super 8’s or within the 2 star motel genre.

The young man smiled and greeted me each time our paths crossed.
He brought his adorable daughter out for a walk in her pretty dress when I was out for a smoke and though irrelevant, as a woman who had the best dad in the world who made everything special,  I always find it touching to observe a dad creating small moments with a daughter she’ll remember forever as I do, 50 years later.

The effort of providing this high level of service and attention to detail within the limits of the 2 star price point should be rewarded.

There's also a handicap parking spot right by the boat launch. They only allow electric motors, so we had no problems with obnoxious speed boaters, just quiet fishermen. There's a small island in the middle of the lake that was loaded with birds, mostly Canadian geese. On the far side of the lake, I found a massive snapping turtle surrounded by dozens of painted turtles. To the right side, there's a shallow opening where the creek feeds the lake. We ventured down it, around many downed trees, even scooting our kayaks over one to get to the dam that created the stream. There were dozens of huge fish there, too! I tried to capture them on camera but was largely unsuccessful. A couple of fishermen on a larger boat got as close as they could, but the big ones were right up close to the dam, far out of reach of anyone not in a kayak. Even a canoe would be too wide to get through.
